props.literal: A little tool I built because I was tired of fighting with PDF headers and footers.
Free to use. Not planning to monetise it.
Cover page showing a footer that makes no sense there
Page numbers that just won't skip page one
Same header pasted into every template, by hand
Every section wanting slightly different rules
Each page, or range of pages, can carry its own header and footer rule — right there in the schema. No post-processing step, no hacky workaround glued on afterwards.
That's genuinely most of it. Write the JSON, see it live on the canvas, export a proper print-ready PDF at the end.
Everything validates as you type — so there's no nasty surprise waiting at export time.
The bit I'm actually proud of
Show a header only on odd pages, or only the first / last
Pin a rule to one exact page number if you need to
"Page X of Y" numbering, done automatically
Hide a footer on just the cover page
It all sits in the schema itself, so the same JSON prints correctly whether you're previewing it, exporting it, or handing it off to a teammate.
Drag and drop. Or just write JSON.
If JSON is more your thing
Both stay in sync — change one, the other updates on its own.
The engine measures elements offscreen first, then decides where to break. You never add a manual page break anywhere.
You can just ask it, honestly
— pin a rule to one exact page
postMessage / window events for talking across the frame
your end users edit and print their own copy
Need a clean invoice, certificate or report and don't want to open a design tool for it? This is basically for you.
Want your users to tweak and print their own documents from your schema? Embed it, and hand over the reins.
Either way, it's your schema — and now it's theirs too.
Something like "hide this if total > 0" — beyond the built-in page conditions.
Right now a schema mistake throws a raw Ajv error. Wants to read like plain English instead.
Most of my recent releases were deployment fixes, not features — want that to stop being true.
As more people start using this, I'd like a clear way for folks to pitch in.
This entire document was built by an AI agent.
> User: "lets create a new page like : screen which reveals about capability of this builder"
> Agent: Successfully replaced document body children and passed validation.

Because PaperCast is driven entirely by a strict JSON schema, you don't even need to use the visual playground. You can plug the schema into an LLM with the provided MCP server, and it can build, iterate, and refine the layout autonomously.
If your tool outputs a clean, predictable data structure, AI agents can use it like a native API.

It's free, it's open, and I'm not planning to charge for it.
Would genuinely love to know what you think.
